I have been growing chrysanthemum on this 35 mu plot for more than ten years now, and last year I got about 300 kg of dried flowers per mu. The market price was good — 60 yuan per kg — so I am not changing my basic approach this year. I start by rotary tilling the whole field in early April. For planting, I use improved cuttings, about 2,750 plants per mu, which I buy from the nursery. I have learned over the years that flowers need a balanced diet, so my base fertilizer is 150 kg per mu of general compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind — which gives me 22.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium right from the start. Then I topdress once with 40 kg per mu of urea, adding another 18 kg of nitrogen when the buds are forming. That brings my total to about 40 kg of nitrogen, 22 kg of phosphorus, and 22 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate four times through the season using my well and border irrigation — once right after planting, once in June when it gets hot, and twice in August and September when the flowers are setting. For chemicals, I spray insecticide four times and herbicide twice; I skip fungicide this year unless I see mildew, which I did not have last year. My expected yield is 300 kg per mu again. I run this mostly by myself since it is just me in the household, but for 35 mu I hire a few people during harvest. Every yuan counts on this scale, but I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing half my yield to poor flowering.
